text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Prime Minister Kim Campbell unlikely to testify: Somalia commissioners say inquiry will be unable to hear from high-ranking players.
- Ontario to revamp school system: Local boards losing control.
- Elusive black holes almost a sure thing: Astrophysicists tracking down quarry.
- Tax credit to target child poverty: Next federal budget to allot funds.
- Swift Current's hockey glory turns to ashes: In this small city where the Broncos rule, the sex-abuse scandal created by a once revered coach has residents agonizing.
- Canadian 88 makes bids for Morrison: Natural gas driller launches C$652-million hostile takeover despite target firm's poison pill.
- New choppers spark doubts: Can rescue fleet do the same job.
- Bre-X releases rich drill results on Busang field: High grade of gold may force Barrick to sweeten bid on Indonesian deposit.
- Hydro-Quebec pays C$309-million for Gaz Metro stake: Team up for concerted push into U.S.
- Canadian 88 makes C$652-million play for Morrison: Surprise offer must overcome Morrison Petroleum's newly instituted poison pill and possibly an army of white knights.
- New Bre-X results glitter, but for whom?
